title: Meeting Ellington at the Orpheum and the $70 salary
summary: Ellington said he had never heard him but Mills said to hire him; Brown took $70 a week to see the East.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Who else was -- worked at the Cotton Club with you, at the same time you were working there with Hite Lionel Hampton and Les Height? About the time you quit.
Gee, I forgot who was in the band. Humph, you know that's almost 50 years ago? I mean, who can remember 50 years? That's pretty hard. I really can't call names off, you know, quickly.
So when Irving Mills hired you, Duke was appearing here at the Orpheum?
Had You met Duke at that time?

No, the first time I saw him was the next day, and the next day, which was Wednesday, I went down. He told me to come down to the Orpheum Theater, and I went down there. And he says, "I never knew you," Duke says, "I never knew you, I never met you, I never heard you. But Irving says get you, so that's that." So, well, "How much you paying?" Well, now, I had never been East, and I always looked at a thing that gave me an opportunity to do something that I wanted to do, wasn't so much the money. It was the something that I thought would be advantageous to my life or my career. So when everybody else fell over when he quoted the price to me, I said, "Well, I want to take a trip East. I'll be back next year." So I started with Duke Ellington for $70.00 a week. And the band fell off their chairs.
